name: Glossa.live
description: Live voice translation for churches, conferences and events into 100+ languages; listeners hear or read the translation on their own phones, "no headsets required", "no equipment needed" (company-stated). Homepage claims it is "used by hundreds of churches all over the world" and shows SBC, Hillsong, PCA, CCA, UMC logos (company-stated). Pricing: Pay As You Go $5/hour/language, Standard $99/mo, Advanced $299/mo, Premium $499/mo (founder-stated). ~2,000 estimated users (founder-stated). Founded Jun 2025, Cyprus, founder Anton K. 100 active subscriptions; L30 profit margin 65%. Yes, it's AI under the hood, but the buyer is a church tech volunteer and the job is "make Sunday work in Spanish and Ukrainian".

No cliff. Revenue synced 19 October 2026 ~04:53 Warsaw.
mentions.indieAngle: Same "live captions/translation to phones" product for another weekly gathering with a budget: Polish parishes with Ukrainian congregants, city council sessions, trade fairs, university lectures. Sell per hour, then move them onto a monthly plan.

whyItPrints: It replaces interpreter booths and headset rentals, a real line item for churches. Churches run every week, so usage repeats. It sells by word of mouth inside denominations, and once the Sunday workflow is set up nobody switches.
